spec.title: APP-STEPS campaign v0.1 — structured installation with agent steps

status.comment: Opened 2026-10-31 on local main after APP-CLEAN closed.

p.mandate: Owner, 2026-10-31, verbatim: «Попробуй обдумать всю эту схему и написать самый лучший на свете инсталлятор с агентами», with the two framing messages of the same day: pre- and post-agent steps with a package-authored prompt, a user-configured agent from the supported harness set, interactive or unattended, an externally registered agent command for automation, tested first with a fake script and then with the owner's `~/opt/bin/claude-codex` wrapper; multi-stage installers in the InstallShield / NSIS tradition with conditions on whether a step runs, designed so that a graphical editor can soon author them and so that people and agents like using the result; and the rule «всегда должна быть возможность делать инсталляторы целиком БЕЗ агентов»: agent steps are skipped with an upfront warning when no agent is configured.

p.baseline: Local `main` at `4d7307f69` after APP-CLEAN: `vibe-app` 5 9xx lines, one-method installer options, hooks, source builds, storage, project scope; full gate green (AUDIT 2026-10-31). Contracts: PROP-064 (agent hooks) and PROP-065 (structured installation), both accepted by `vibe check`.

p.decision-sugar: D1 — every existing method is the short spelling of a step list; the engine runs steps only. Rejected: two engines (methods and steps) side by side.

p.decision-data: D2 — closed kind set, closed condition vocabulary, a planner that answers before downloading, a kept work directory with `steps.json` and `--resume`. Rejected: a transactional engine, an expression language, steps spawning steps.

p.decision-agent: D3 — an agent is a command plus argument templates (presets as data, user overrides, external registration through `VIBE_AGENT_COMMAND`), delivered by spawn, by the registered command, or by parking inside a hosting agent; never nested, never an API call, never without the prompt shown and consent given; always skippable with a warning.

p.phase-q1: Q1 — the step engine: manifest model (features, steps, kinds, conditions, needs, templates, result), sugar mapping, planner and `vibe app plan` / `--plan-only` / `vibe app steps`, runner with `steps.json`, `--resume` / `--from-step`, index record of features and outcomes, reverse uninstall, `copy` kind; the `agent` kind is parsed, planned as skipped-without-agent and refused when `required`. Gate: PROP-065 acceptance fixtures minus the agent-specific ones; every existing fixture unchanged.

p.phase-q1b: Q1b — the wizard surface (owner, 2026-10-31: «подумай ещё что может не хватать графическому мастеру от нашего движка, всё реализуй»): `describe`, the feature tree with relations and profiles (`--profile`, resolution rules, indented multi-select), parameters with `--set` and typed prompts, license acceptance, declared input sizes with plan totals and byte progress, the application icon, run records with per-step logs and `vibe app runs`, cancellation that forwards the signal and leaves a resume point, the JSON progress stream (`PROP-060#MACHINE-STREAM`), error codes in the JSON envelope and `vibe app errors`, the exit-code table. Gate: a fixture driving the engine the way a tool would — `describe` → `plan` with `--set` and `--feature` → `install --json --progress-format json --assume-yes --accept-license` parsing the event stream → a killed install recorded `interrupted` and resumed → `runs` listing the log.

p.phase-q2: Q2 (after Q1b) — agent hooks: `agents.toml`, presets, selection order, external registration, modes, consent, envelope, answer, parking and resume, transcript record, `vibe agent list|presets`, `vibe app hooks`. Gate: PROP-064 acceptance fixture with a fake agent executable; MT-06 with the owner's `claude-codex` wrapper.

p.phase-q3: Q3 — maintenance verbs, packages and close-out: hidden installations (`PROP-059#hidden-installations`: `--hidden`, `app expose|hide`, `shell --with`, owner question of 2026-10-31), application dependencies (`PROP-065#app-dependencies`, build scope by default, tree removal per `PROP-065#uninstall-tree`, update keeping the previous version hidden with rollback and hold per `PROP-065#update-and-rollback`, owner question of 2026-10-31: a MinGW package the Vim source build optionally depends on) with a published `org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64` package, the `env` step kind (`PROP-065#env-step`, owner question of 2026-10-31 on installers that set environment variables and remove them on uninstall), `vibe app modify` and `vibe app outdated` (`PROP-065#modify`, `#outdated`; the owner's 2026-10-31 question: change any installed choice later, such as a source build for a binary, and let updates follow the recorded choice); the Vim bridge and the documentation site rewritten as step lists (Vim with an optional agent step under a feature), documentation, changelog, full gate, audit entry, report.

p.mandate-goal: Owner, 2026-10-31, `/goal`: «доделай всё про инсталляцию пакетов (кроме графического приложения). Сделай пакет vim уже на новом движке. Проверь его на Windows (компьютер base … современный powershell и все команды сразу же выполняются с привилегиями администратора) и mac (компьютер flash) … ты можешь добавить в PATH все что нужно и скачивать новые ништяки в C:/opt. Для Mac все то же самое, но директория ~/opt. Когда проверишь, что всё работает и vim реально запускается, опубликуй его и дальше запушь и опубликуй vibevm 1.0.8.» This authorises the outward actions: publishing the Vim bridge to the registry, pushing `main` through the mirror procedure, and the 1.0.8 release — each only after its verification.

p.phase-n: N — native verification on the owner's machines over SSH: `base` (Windows 11, PowerShell 7, admin; toolchains may be downloaded into `C:\opt` and put on PATH) and `flash` (macOS 15 Intel, Command Line Tools). Build the vibe bundle for each target, install the Vim package through every option that applies (Windows ZIP, Windows source if a compiler can be provisioned, macOS source), run Vim, run the MT-04 / MT-05 steps that automation can run, record the evidence in the ledger.

p.phase-r: R — release: publish the Vim bridge (`vibe registry publish`), full gate, changelog and version `1.0.8`, tag, mirror push, distribution bundles through `cargo xtask dist` and the release workflow, final verification of an install from the published registry.

p.ledger-q1b: Q1b landed as `507542530` (87 files, +7809/-1047). Review: feature resolution records which rule implied each feature; the error-code table is macro-generated with an exhaustive match; signal handling carries documented unsafe gates on both unix and Windows; the JSON renderer never writes stdout. Boss fixes: the tee test asserted an order between stdout and stderr that two pump threads do not guarantee; `tests_application.rs` had crossed the 600-line cap by the boss's own earlier commit. Gate on the committed tree: fmt, `cargo test --workspace` (after the fix), clippy `-D warnings`, `vibe check` (0 errors), conform (0 new), check-codegen clean, wire-diff green with 7 shifted paths under the pre-publication regime. Deviations the worker named (profile replaces defaults; license asked first; CLI `bail!` argument errors still exit 1; no step tasks in the interactive renderer because of a suspend_progress deadlock risk) are accepted as the simplest readings.

p.ledger: 2026-10-31: PROP-064 and PROP-065 written, campaign opened, Q1 dispatched. Later the same day: the wizard-surface anchors added to PROP-065 and PROP-060 and phase Q1b inserted before Q2.
